reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Isolated thrombocytopenia with large platelets and well patient means ITP pattern
Palpable purpura means vasculitis; flat petechiae mean platelet problem
Glanzmann lacks aggregation receptor IIb IIIa; Bernard Soulier lacks adhesion Ib with giant platelets
Aspirin disables platelet COX irreversibly for the platelet lifespan
reference.pathophysiology: Autoantibodies opsonise platelets for splenic macrophages while megakaryocyte production also falters in ITP. Receptor or granule defects break adhesion, aggregation or secretion steps of primary haemostasis, and vessel wall inflammation or collagen failure leaks blood despite perfect platelets, explaining normal count bleeding.
additionalDifferentials: ITP versus marrow failure versus sequestration thrombocytopenia
Glanzmann versus Bernard Soulier receptor defects
Vasculitic palpable versus thrombocytopenic flat purpura
additionalInvestigations: Blood count with film (exclude schistocytes and blasts urgently)
Marrow examination in atypical, older or multilineage cases
Platelet function and von Willebrand testing in normal count bleeding
